findings.summary: continuous_proof and evidence_kind are derived from certificate.proven alone, not from admission. A strict-mode report that is NOT admitted (because the sampled gate rejected it) can therefore carry continuous_proof=True and evidence_kind='convex_hull_span_certified', contradicting the in-scope contract document ('continuous_proof (True only on a strict pass)') and the report dataclass docstring, and contradicting the 'strict path PASS' paragraph. Every such report is a rejection (fail-closed), and no in-repo consumer reads continuous_proof for authorization, so there is no safety effect.

evidence.math_note: Proven certificate implies the mathematical sampled gate (the radius+required offset of a convex box is convex, so chords between two cleared points stay cleared; the inset box is convex), so the mismatch is reachable only through floating-point rounding at the boundary - which is exactly what these three witnesses are.

findings.summary: The contract documents each intervals tuple as (start_u, end_u, first_active_index, last_active_index), but the implementation appends (interval_start, interval_end, index, last) where index is the SPAN index j, not the first active control-point index. For order p the two differ by p (first_active = j - p), so a consumer following the document would read the wrong control points (P_3.. instead of P_0.. for the first interval of a cubic). The in-repo test reads the field with the true convention (`_points[first - 3:last + 1]`), so behaviour is correct; only the published field description is wrong.

evidence.probe: probe_1_cover_index.py check 'third field is span j (not first_active); j-p == 0' over 96 layouts; observed first interval tuple (0.0, 0.1, 3, 3) for N=4 (first_active 0, span j 3)

findings.summary: The module docstring step 2 and docs/plan/102-trajectory-scene-admission-contract.md:150-154 claim that repeated left knots 'widen the active set, which keeps the bound sound' and that degenerate zero-length spans are 'skipped, never fused'. In fact the strict-monotonicity gate at lines 386-389 returns non_monotone_knots for ANY repeated knot before the walk, so the grouping branch (lines 406-411) and the zero-length-span skip are unreachable dead code; the stated soundness rationale is never exercised. Behaviour is still fail-closed (a repeating vector proves nothing and is rejected), and no repeated-knot vector can even be constructed through EgoSpline/bridge_bspline, so this is a claim/code mismatch, not a safety hole. The in-scope test narrative ('defence-in-depth path ... see test_non_monotone_knots_fail_closed for the tamper case') is likewise inaccurate: the tamper case fails at the monotone gate and never reaches the grouping.

evidence.dynamic_dead_branch_proof: probe_4_knot_boundaries.py locates the source lines by text and counts executed lines with sys.settrace: monotone return = line 388, walk enter = 404, skip continue = 408, grouping loop = 410, grouping step = 411, active slice = 412. For six cardinality-preserving repeating vectors (interior, second span, domain start, last span, pre-domain, doubled) the monotone return executes and 408/410/411/412 never do; interval_count is 0 and proven False in every case.
evidence.evaluator_out_of_contract: the FP evaluator itself raises SplineError (degenerate knot interval / division by zero) on the tampered second-span repeat, so repeated-knot evaluation is not even well defined in this pipeline
evidence.upstream_evidence: Modules/ego_planner_swarm/bspline_opt/src/uniform_bspline.cpp:44 setKnot performs no validation; the repo's bridge/EgoSpline boundary is what rejects repeats (ego_evaluator.py:88-90)

findings.minimal_patch: Prefer wording (option a): Simulator/wksim_planning/ego_scene_admission.py:320-323 replace the repeated-knot soundness sentence with 'Any non-strictly-increasing (repeated or non-monotone) knot vector is rejected fail-closed as non_monotone_knots BEFORE the walk, so every interval that reaches the walk is a plain strictly-increasing span whose active window is P_{j-p}..P_j (c == j); the grouping/degenerate-span handling below is defensive only.'; docs/plan/102-trajectory-scene-admission-contract.md:150-154 likewise; validation/test_ego_scene_admission.py:517-523 reword the docstring to state the branch is unreachable even under tampering (or delete the now-unused grouping code, which is the cleanest option since no input can reach it). Option b (relax the gate to non-decreasing to activate the grouping) is not recommended: the evaluator cannot evaluate repeats (de Boor denominator zero) and the pipeline's EgoSpline boundary rejects them anyway.

findings.summary: ADMISSION_REASONS has 12 members; _ADMISSION_REASON_TO_OUTCOME has 8. The four unmapped ones (invalid_adapter, invalid_binding, invalid_anchor, invalid_spline) are constructor-only or unreachable through admit(), which probe_5 confirms, so today the table is complete for every reachable reason. But the lookup uses `_ADMISSION_REASON_TO_OUTCOME.get(error.reason, 'rejected_adapter')`, so a future admission reason that is added to ADMISSION_REASONS without a mapping row is silently mislabelled as an adapter rejection instead of failing loudly; docs/plan/102-trajectory-scene-admission-contract.md:277 ('maps every reason to a pump outcome') is only vacuously true.

evidence.probe: probe_5_atomicity_pump_outcomes.py: all eight mapped reasons were triggered end to end through admit()/pump.feed and observed; reachable == {identity_mismatch, invalid_mapping, bridge_rejected, invalid_grid, clearance_violation, continuous_clearance_unproven, map_violation, adapter_rejected}; unmapped == {invalid_adapter, invalid_binding, invalid_anchor, invalid_spline}

findings.summary: The document says '(40 tests)' for validation/test_ego_scene_admission.py; the suite contains and runs 41 tests (15 + 15 + 11).

The _aabb_gap docstring says 'All terms are exact real quantities; only the final sqrt rounds once.' The per-axis subtractions a_low - b_high / b_lo - a_high are correctly rounded but not exact in general, the three squares and the two additions each round, and the sqrt rounds last. The measured deviation from the exact box-box distance is nevertheless small (worst 1.35 ulp over 3000 random box pairs), so this is a precision-wording nit, not a soundness issue.
findings.evidence: probe_2_clearance_accounting.py check 'aabb_gap matches the exact box-box distance (<= 4 ulp)' measured worst_ulp_error = 1.3483018972989647
findings.minimal_patch: Reword to 'Per axis the separation is computed with correctly rounded subtractions; the Euclidean norm is then assembled with three squares, two additions and one sqrt, so the result is within a few ulp of the exact real distance (measured worst case 1.35 ulp).'

findings.summary: The certificate is described as tiling the 'exact clamped domain [u_p, u_{m-p}]'. The domain is the upstream getTimeSpan domain; the real EGO layout is NOT clamped (uniform_bspline.cpp:29-41 leaves u_0..u_{p-1} below and u_{m-p+1}..u_m above the domain), and a genuinely clamped vector (end multiplicity p+1) would need repeated knots, which EgoSpline and the certificate's monotone gate both reject. The code is correct for every constructible layout - the word 'clamped' is the only inaccuracy.
findings.evidence: probe_4_knot_boundaries.py: clamped candidate rejected at EgoSpline construction; upstream knots show u0 < u_p and u_m > u_m-p; probe_1 verifies cover == [u_p, u_{m-p}] for uniform, non-uniform, shifted and extreme-aspect layouts
findings.minimal_patch: Replace 'exact clamped domain' with 'exact evaluation domain [u_p, u_{m-p}] (= upstream getTimeSpan)' in the module docstring and in docs/plan/102-trajectory-scene-admission-contract.md:150.

findings.summary: On a structural certificate failure the violation mapping carries clearance = -inf and envelope_clearance = -inf (min_net_obstacle_clearance / min_hull_inset_clearance default to -math.inf). The report is in-memory only today and no in-repo consumer serializes it, but a future evidence writer using json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) would raise on such a report. Reported for information only; no change required for this slice.

verified_claims.detail: 96 layouts x full tuple equality against the independently computed spec; worst curve excursion outside its claimed active-set AABB = 8.88e-16 m (FP evaluation noise).

verified_claims.claim: Domain coverage: the interval cover is exactly [knots[p], knots[N]] == [u_p, u_{m-p}], gap-free, contiguous, and its span equals EgoSpline.duration.
verified_claims.detail: Checked for uniform, lengthenTime-shaped non-uniform, log-uniform random gaps (1e-6..1e3), shifted domains (u_p != 0), and extreme h (1e-6, 50).

verified_claims.claim: Soundness premise: the curve stays inside the AABB of the active points its own interval claims.
verified_claims.detail: 65 samples per interval over all layouts; max excess 8.88e-16 m.

verified_claims.claim: proven == True never coexists with a MATERIAL curve intrusion.
verified_claims.detail: No obstacle or inset violation beyond 1e-9 m. The only strict (exact-predicate) hits are at the razor boundary y = nextafter(1.65) with worst exact slack -2.78e-16 m, i.e. the FP evaluation/boundary noise floor ~2.5 ulp, 15 orders of magnitude below the 0.65 m margin. This is a counterexample search, not a proof.

verified_claims.claim: Net clearance formula: gap(box, obstacle) - vehicle_radius >= required_clearance, with each term applied exactly once (no duplicated radius, no dropped radius).
verified_claims.detail: reported gap == independently recomputed min box gap; net == gap - radius bitwise; empirical obstacle accept threshold 0.6500000000000001 m and inset threshold 0.6499999999999999 m versus the exact double-sum margin 0.649999999999999967 (< 1 ulp), which rules out the 1.00 m (2r+req) and 0.30 m (required only) signatures.

verified_claims.claim: The certificate's obstacle measure equals the sampled path's centreline measure (no scale/unit mismatch).
verified_claims.detail: For a constant curve the certificate gap is bitwise equal to scene_profile.segment_surface_distance(p, p).

verified_claims.claim: Map inset is per axis and uses margin = vehicle_radius + required_clearance.
verified_claims.detail: _inset_clearance returns three signed axes; a single-axis intrusion of -0.65 m is rejected even though the cross-axis mean is +4.02 m; the decision is a plain >= 0 on the minimum axis value.

verified_claims.claim: Float threshold semantics: the acceptance comparison is '>=', deterministic, and never materially permissive.
verified_claims.detail: 13-step ulp ladder around the exact margin on both gates; worst exact slack of any ADMITTED report is at the FP noise floor; no admitted report is materially inside the margin.

verified_claims.claim: Strict/legacy compatibility: legacy mode keeps sampled_segment_checked / continuous_proof=False / continuous_certificate=None and still admits the audit witness.
verified_claims.detail: Sampled evidence numbers are identical in both modes on the same spline; only the strict path adds the certificate.

verified_claims.claim: Failure atomicity: every rejection path calls the adapter zero times and leaves the session snapshot unchanged.
verified_claims.detail: identity_mismatch, invalid_mapping, bridge_rejected, invalid_grid, clearance_violation, map_violation, continuous_clearance_unproven, adapter_rejected: 0 adapter calls and unchanged (state, generation, last_event_sequence, last_command_id, identity) for the admission gates; adapter_rejected is the only path that calls the adapter twice (once per attempt) and still rolls back.

verified_claims.claim: A strict rejection burns no event sequence and does not block the next valid trajectory.
verified_claims.detail: After a committed activation, the witness is rejected as continuous_clearance_unproven and the immediately following valid frame activates with the SAME event sequence; at the pump level the same sequence is reused by the next clear frame.
